blocks.body: The conventional target is three to six months of essential expenses — not of income — held in an insured, liquid account. Start with a starter fund of $1,000 or one month of expenses so a small surprise does not become new debt, then build to the full target after the employer match and high-interest debt. Size toward the high end, or beyond it, when income is variable, when one earner supports the household, when there are dependents, or when re-employment in your field is slow.
blocks.plain: The usual target is three to six months of essential costs — not of income — kept in an insured account you can reach quickly. Start with a small fund of $1,000 or one month of costs, so a small surprise doesn't become new debt. Then build to the full target after getting your employer match and paying off high-interest debt. Aim higher, or beyond the range, if your income goes up and down, if one person supports the household, if you have dependents, or if finding a new job in your field takes a long time.

blocks.body: Health coverage is a Tier-1 item in the plan for a reason: one uninsured hospital stay can turn a stable budget into unpayable debt. ACA-compliant plans cap in-network out-of-pocket spending each year (2026 cap: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family); that cap, not the premium, is the number your cash reserves should aim to cover. If that is out of reach, check whether you qualify for Medicaid, whose rules vary by state, or for cost-sharing reductions, which lower the cap on a Marketplace silver plan. Nonprofit hospitals must have a written financial assistance policy; ask for it before paying a large bill.
blocks.plain: Health coverage is a Tier-1 (top-priority) step for a reason: one hospital stay without insurance can turn a steady budget into debt you can't pay. ACA-compliant plans limit what you pay in-network each year (2026 limit: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family). That limit, not the premium, is the amount your savings should aim to cover. If that is out of reach, check whether you qualify for Medicaid (the rules differ by state) or for cost-sharing reductions, which lower the limit on a Marketplace silver plan. Nonprofit hospitals must have a written financial assistance policy. Ask for it before you pay a large bill.

blocks.body: For a working adult, disability is more likely than early death, and an earner's future income is usually their largest asset. Group long-term disability commonly replaces about 60% of base salary; if your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxable, which lowers the real replacement rate. The policy features that decide whether a claim pays — own-occupation versus any-occupation definition, the elimination period, the benefit period — matter as much as the percentage.
blocks.plain: For someone who works, becoming disabled is more likely than dying early, and your future pay is usually your biggest asset. Group long-term disability insurance often replaces about 60% of base pay. If your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxed, so you really get less. The policy details that decide whether a claim pays — whether "disabled" means unable to do your own job or any job, how long you wait before benefits start, how long benefits last — matter as much as the percentage.

Future income is usually the largest asset
Group LTD commonly replaces ~60% of base salary
Employer-paid premium → taxable benefit → lower real replacement
Own-occ vs any-occ, elimination period, benefit period matter as much

blocks.body: Life insurance replaces income for people who depend on it; with no dependents it is rarely needed. The common heuristic for a primary earner with dependents is 10–12 times annual income; the DIME method (debt + income for the years needed + mortgage + education) gives a household-specific number. Term coverage is the default for this job; whole-life policies bundle insurance with a low-return savings component.

A common rule of thumb for a main earner with dependents is 10–12 times yearly income; the DIME method (debt + income for the years needed + mortgage + education) gives a number for your household. Term insurance is the standard choice for this job. Whole-life policies bundle insurance with a savings part that earns little.

blocks.body: A landlord's policy covers the building, not the tenant's belongings or the tenant's liability; renters insurance covers both. Homeowners should insure to the cost of rebuilding rather than market value, and should know that standard policies exclude flood damage.

blocks.body: State minimum liability limits are set low and can leave your savings exposed after a serious accident. Consumer guidance commonly suggests at least $100,000 per person, $300,000 per accident and $100,000 property damage; umbrella carriers usually require higher underlying limits before they will write a policy.

blocks.body: An umbrella policy adds liability coverage on top of auto and homeowners policies. It is inexpensive per dollar of coverage — industry pricing surveys put $1 million at roughly $200–400 a year — and is commonly sized to at least your net worth.

blocks.body: Beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance pass those assets directly and generally override a will, so they are the first thing to check. A will directs everything else and is where parents name a guardian for minor children; without one, state intestacy law decides. A durable financial power of attorney lets someone you choose manage your finances if you cannot; without one, a family may need a court-appointed guardian or conservator. A healthcare directive (living will plus a healthcare proxy) records your medical wishes and who decides, and a HIPAA authorization lets named people get your medical information. Each is governed by state law.
blocks.plain: Beneficiary forms on retirement accounts and life insurance send that money straight to the people named, and they usually win over a will — so check them first. A will covers everything else, and it is where parents name a guardian for young children; without one, your state's law decides who gets what. A durable financial power of attorney lets a person you choose handle your money if you can't; without one, your family may need a court to appoint someone. A healthcare directive (a living will plus a healthcare proxy) records the care you want and who decides for you, and a HIPAA authorization lets people you name get your medical information. State law governs each of these.

blocks.body: A security freeze stops new credit being opened in your name and is free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion; it does not affect your credit score, and you can lift it temporarily when you apply for credit. You can pull your own reports free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov builds the recovery plan, and reporting unauthorized electronic transfers to your bank quickly limits your liability.
blocks.plain: A security freeze stops anyone from opening new credit in your name. It's free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, it doesn't change your credit score, and you can lift it for a while when you apply for credit. You can check your own credit reports for free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov makes a recovery plan for you, and telling your bank quickly about electronic transfers you didn't make limits how much you can lose.
